summary: Fixture reduced from a real audit run

report.healthVerdict: The core (transactions, state machine, credentials) is well built and fails closed. Its defects sit at the edges: inconsistent fault classification, scope enforcement by convention, incomplete cascade side-effects, and a few hot-spot files every feature edits. Nothing found is critical or high.
report.executiveSummary: Seven reviewers (4 slices, 3 lenses) kept 65 findings: 19 medium, 46 low, none critical or high. 17 are CONFIRMED and 48 UNVERIFIED; 3 were refuted. Strengths: a single transaction owner (UnitRunner), a data-driven state machine with a pure gate order, hash-only fail-closed credentials, scope that never reveals whether an item exists, and one dispatcher for MCP and REST. Problems: faults are classified in several places that disagree, and some INTERNAL outcomes are never logged (R04, R05, R13-R16). Scope is enforced per handler, with one confirmed SSE leak (R01). Run and cascade side-effects are incomplete (R02, R08, R22). Fail-open defaults pass the compiler (R20, R24, R27, R29). AdvanceService, YamlSchemaParser and CurrentMcpServer are hot spots (R09, R10, R50). Do first: R01, R02, R04, R05, R06, R07, R03, and verify R11 and R28.

themes.name: T1 Fault classification has no single owner
themes.summary: PersistenceFaults, LegacyFaults, ScopeGuard's catch-all and ApiStatusPages classify the same faults differently, some INTERNAL outcomes go unlogged, and config-fault capture is copied by hand. Remedy: one FaultTranslator port, one logging point, config exceptions passed through UnitRunner, a per-element catch in BatchRunner.

themes.name: T2 Scope enforcement is a per-handler convention
themes.summary: Capability is declared on the spec and checked centrally; root and tag scope is applied by hand in about 70 handlers, the SSE loop and the direct routes. Remedy: a scope rule declared on every SelectSpec and OpSpec, a registry-wide restricted-scope sweep test, and a JWKS default that denies by scope.

themes.name: T3 Fail-open defaults on wiring parameters
themes.summary: Security-relevant constructor and dispatch parameters default to off, LOCAL or a fresh instance, so leaving one unwired still compiles. Remedy: no defaults in production constructors; named constants and test builders for the off cases.

strengths: A single transaction owner keeps writes atomic (see R04 for the batch edge).
Credentials are stored as hashes and fail closed.

now: Close the SSE scope leak (R01) and the fail-open defaults (R20).
next: One fault translator for every route (R15, R04).

report.method: Seven reviewers read four slices and three lenses; every finding was merged, then one agent tried to refute it where the cap allowed.

kept.title: Type-only schema view omits the type's default_traits notes and seats, disagreeing with what an item of that type is gated on
kept.evidence: Resolving a type-only schema view returns fewer notes than the schema an item of that type is gated on.
kept.impact: Callers that read the type schema to prepare an item miss the default_traits notes and seats, then hit a gate they were never told about.
kept.recommendation: Resolve the type view through the same trait merge the item view uses, and add a test that both views agree.

kept.title: Integer env vars parse silently with no range check; API_SSE_AUTH_CHECK_INTERVAL_SECONDS <= 0 busy-spins a thread per SSE connection
kept.evidence: Integer environment variables are parsed without a range check; a zero or negative SSE auth interval is accepted.
kept.impact: A zero interval makes each SSE connection spin a thread, so one misconfigured variable degrades the whole server.
kept.recommendation: Parse integers through one bounded helper that rejects values outside a documented range at startup.

kept.title: Per-element batch: a non-persistence exception in element N turns the whole call into internal after elements 0..N-1 committed
kept.evidence: BatchRunner catches only persistence faults per element, so any other exception escapes after earlier elements committed.
kept.impact: A caller sees an internal error for the whole call although part of the batch was applied.
kept.recommendation: Catch per element and report the failing index with the partial results.

kept.title: AdvanceService hot spot: one 1,489-line class owns policy mapping, apply, cascades, leases, typed-block validation and legacy messages
kept.evidence: AdvanceService is one class of roughly fifteen hundred lines that mixes policy mapping, apply, cascades and leases.
kept.impact: Every feature that touches transitions edits this file, which raises merge conflicts and review cost.
kept.recommendation: Extract cascade and lease handling behind the existing service seam, one concern per step.

kept.title: Fail-open constructor defaults on AdvanceService silently disable seat enforcement, leases and pins when a parameter is not wired
kept.evidence: Constructor parameters for seat enforcement, leases and pins default to off.
kept.impact: A new construction site that omits a parameter compiles and silently disables the check.
kept.recommendation: Make the parameters required, or default them to the enforcing value.

kept.title: SSE tag-scope cache is never refreshed when ?types= drops item.* events, so access lost through a tag change keeps streaming
kept.evidence: The SSE loop caches tag scope once and never refreshes it when item events are filtered out.
kept.impact: A consumer that lost access through a tag change keeps receiving events.
kept.recommendation: Refresh the scope cache on a timer independent of the event filter.

kept.title: A JWT without to_scope is unrestricted across every project root
kept.evidence: A token without a scope claim is treated as unrestricted across every project root.
kept.impact: Any issuer that omits the claim grants cross-project access.
kept.recommendation: Deny by default when the claim is absent, behind a documented setting.

kept.title: Root/tag scope enforcement relies on each tool handler calling ScopeGuard, with no registry-wide guard
locations: current/src/main/kotlin/io/github/jpicklyk/mcptask/current/application/support/ScopeGuard.kt (KDoc: 'Tool handlers call it for every item an op touches (the dispatcher cannot...)')
current/src/main/kotlin/io/github/jpicklyk/mcptask/current/interfaces/shared/tools/ToolDispatcher.kt:dispatch (capability checked centrally, scope only passed through as CallContext.scope)
kept.evidence: Root and tag scope checks depend on each handler calling the guard.
kept.impact: A new handler that forgets the call ships without scope enforcement and no test fails.
kept.recommendation: Declare a scope rule on every operation spec and sweep the registry in one test.

kept.title: REST routes outside the dispatcher do not translate persistence faults: a busy database is 500 internal there but retryable unavailable on /ops
kept.evidence: Routes outside the dispatcher do not translate persistence faults.
kept.impact: A busy database is a 500 on those routes but a retryable error on the dispatcher.
kept.recommendation: Route every fault through the one translator.

kept.title: Start and reopen cascades climb only one level, leaving a terminal grandparent with an active descendant
locations: current/src/main/kotlin/io/github/jpicklyk/mcptask/current/domain/lifecycle/TransitionPolicy.kt:456-471 (followUps: only User triggers emit Start/Reopen cascades)
current/src/main/kotlin/io/github/jpicklyk/mcptask/current/domain/lifecycle/TransitionPolicy.kt:490-499 (closedParent: a terminal AUTO parent takes no new children)
kept.evidence: Start and reopen cascades climb a single level.
kept.impact: A terminal grandparent can keep an active descendant.
kept.recommendation: Walk the ancestor chain until a non-terminal parent is found.

kept.title: RunFrontierQueries kdoc says a BLOCKED member waits as manual, but the code reports its typed reason
kept.evidence: A comment says a blocked member waits as manual, but the code reports its typed reason.
kept.impact: Readers trust the comment and misread the frontier output.
kept.recommendation: Correct the comment to match the code.

kept.title: Public-prefix auth bypass matches the raw path with startsWith while the director check is normalization-strict
kept.evidence: The public-prefix check matches the raw path while the director check normalises it.
kept.impact: A path with dot segments could be judged public by one check and not by the other.

LegacyFaults puts raw SQL exception text into client-facing error messages
MCP-over-HTTP tool calls run under the principal snapshot from the session's first bind, not the credential presented on the current request
